presentation.name: Structure Airflow DAGs for safe, cheap imports

Checks the original request was met, not only that the code runs
Reports what was not verified rather than leaving it implied

presentation.name: Write a dashboard FAQ from the workbook, not from memory
presentation.summary: Documents an existing Tableau dashboard from its workbook file and a screenshot of the landing view, taking each metric definition from the workbook rather than inferring one.

Requires a screenshot of the landing view, because the file does not record what a reader of the FAQ sees
Asks for the refresh schedule instead of inferring one from the extract
Describes only the fields the dashboard actually uses, under the captions readers recognise
Hands back the result as a draft with each definition's source, so the owner reviews the gaps rather than the whole document

presentation.name: Repoint a Tableau workbook at a new warehouse safely
presentation.summary: Works out what in a workbook will not survive a connection swap, and proves the dashboard still produces the same numbers afterwards.

Names the rebind outcome that does not announce itself: a field that matches by name and holds something slightly different

Catches the silent breakages: identifier casing, time zones, aliases and groups over changed values, row-level security
Requires reconciliation below the headline total, where two offsetting errors stop cancelling
Stops at what the workbook needs, leaving warehouse redesign as separate work

presentation.name: Translate a metric between SQL and a level-of-detail expression without changing the number
presentation.summary: Rewrites an existing metric in either direction between SQL and a FIXED, INCLUDE or EXCLUDE expression, stating the grains and filter positions the number depends on.
benefits: States both grains — the view's and the expression's — and what happens when the view aggregates the result a second time
Refuses to disguise a rank, a running total or a previous-row lookup as a FIXED expression, because those are table calculations and no grain reproduces them
Names each filter's position, since a dimension filter does not reduce a FIXED expression and a WHERE clause is not automatically a context filter
Returns the missing view instead of guessing one, because INCLUDE and EXCLUDE have no meaning until the sheet's grain is known
Writes the join keys into the SQL direction, where a missing key is a fan-out that leaves every row looking plausible
Hands back the result labelled unchecked until the two expressions have been compared as numbers

presentation.name: Find out why a Tableau dashboard is slow before rewriting it
presentation.summary: Establishes which interaction is slow and where the time actually goes - the queries, Tableau's own compute, or rendering - before anything is rewritten.
benefits: Separates first load, filter changes and tab switches, which rarely share a cause
Splits query time from local compute from rendering, so the fix is attempted in the right place
Checks filter configuration early, where the cost is settings rather than design
Distinguishes a measured cause from a structural hypothesis instead of presenting one as the other
Requires a rewritten calculation to be checked against the original numbers, since Tableau formulas are where confident answers are most often wrong
Names the causes that live outside the workbook and survive any rewrite

presentation.name: Define Pulse metrics so the insight matches the warehouse number

benefits: Binds the metric to a named measure, time column and filter set, instead of to a word that a caption, a calculation and a warehouse column can share
Keeps a ratio as a numerator and a denominator, and refuses to sum a rate, a percentage or a pre-aggregated row
Treats the time column as part of the definition, so order date and ship date are different metrics
Names every filter in force, because data source, extract and metric filters stack and the insight is about whatever survived them
Hands a FIXED field to the SQL-and-LOD translation before accepting it as a measure, because the grain has already collapsed
Records extract versus live, so an insight is not compared with a warehouse that has since moved
Labels an insight unchecked when the comparison cannot be recomputed, instead of treating a well-worded sentence as a check

presentation.name: Assess an inherited Tableau workbook before changing it

Finds the dependencies that break from outside, including custom SQL coupled to warehouse object names
Judges live against extract by what the dashboard is for, rather than calling one of them wrong
States what an audit of the file cannot conclude: correctness, runtime, layout and who uses it

Catches the quiet ones: a context filter, a sort under a table calculation, a parameter default
Keeps a renamed field from being reported as one deletion and one addition
States that a difference is a candidate, and names the comparison that would settle it

presentation.name: Edit technical prose without changing meaning

Replaces unnatural phrasing with how an engineer would actually say it
Flags sentences whose meaning is unclear instead of guessing at them
